rules.heading: # The aim and route review
rules.quote: A plan with an `## Order` has a Standing step that tells its agent to follow this file, by its full path in the live clone: `/root/.claude/hub/aim-review.md`.
rules.says: Every plan that has an Order carries a Standing step telling its agent to follow aim-review.md by the full live-clone path /root/.claude/hub/aim-review.md, and the agent that follows it is the review.

rules.heading: # The aim and route review
rules.quote: Its hand-back is the verdict, and the dispatcher reads that hand-back from the agent's own transcript (`reviewState` in `report.mjs`, `reviewGate` in `hook-dispatch.mjs`). It is never a file
rules.says: The review's verdict is its hand-back, which the dispatcher reads from the agent's own transcript, and it is never written as a file (not even in the scratchpad), because a file would be a verdict nobody gave.
rules.enforcer: reviewState in report.mjs; reviewGate in hook-dispatch.mjs

rules.heading: ## Why a review stands in front of every move
rules.quote: The main thread does not remember a plan. It names the next move from what the agents handed back, and a move chosen that way drifts
rules.says: Because the main thread names each next move from hand-backs and so drifts, a fresh agent that wrote neither the plan nor the work must read each move against the owner's aim and against the guards' own code first and say whether it goes.

rules.heading: ## Who the review is
rules.quote: A fresh agent, on the cheapest model that holds the rules, that wrote neither the plan nor the step it reviews. The model is the plan's choice.
rules.says: The review is a fresh agent on the cheapest model that holds the rules, which wrote neither the plan nor the step it reviews, and the plan chooses the model.

rules.heading: ## Who the review is
rules.quote: It began after everything it judges: after the end of every agent for a step in Order, after the plan's last write, and, while a correction from the owner stands, after that message was typed.
rules.says: A review must begin after the end of every agent for a step in Order, after the plan's last write, and, while an owner correction stands, after that message was typed; a review that began earlier clears nothing and the dispatcher says so.

rules.heading: ## Who the review is
rules.quote: It changes nothing. It reads, runs the one script below, and hands back.
rules.says: The review changes nothing: it only reads, runs the one script given in the file, and hands back.

rules.heading: ## Who the review is
rules.quote: The only command it runs is `node` on that script under `/tmp/claude-0/`; nothing else runs.
rules.says: The only command the review may run is node on the owner-messages script under /tmp/claude-0/, and no other command runs.

rules.heading: ## Who the review is
rules.quote: It never runs the reply guard's release command, `reply-guard.mjs --read`, with or without a value
rules.says: The review never runs reply-guard.mjs --read, with or without a value, because a review has no refusal of its own to read and the no-value form latched a standing review agent (Q-HUB-277).

rules.heading: ## What it reads
rules.quote: By path, never from a summary, because a summary is the paraphrase that drifted.
rules.says: The review reads its sources by path and never from a summary.

rules.heading: ## What it reads
rules.quote: The plan in force. Its path is in the step's prompt.
rules.says: The review reads the plan in force, whose path is given in the step's prompt.

rules.heading: ## What it reads
rules.quote: The report of the step judged, `progress/step-N-report.txt` in the session scratchpad, where N is the step of the newest end of an agent for a step in Order.
rules.says: The review reads progress/step-N-report.txt in the session scratchpad, where N is the step of the newest end of an agent for a step in Order, and N is obtained by running the script with --judged, read the way the gate reads it.

rules.heading: ## What it reads
rules.quote: The manager's notes, `status/manager.txt` in the same scratchpad. Its newest `Next:` line with no number names M, the step whose route is read.
rules.says: The review reads status/manager.txt in the scratchpad, and its newest Next: line with no number names M, the step whose route is read; where it names none, M is the step on the status's next: line.

rules.heading: ## What it reads
rules.quote: The status page's source, `status/fix-run.html`, is not where M is read from, because only a status rewrites its Next line
rules.says: M is never read from status/fix-run.html, because only a status rewrites its Next line and a review that read it judged a step already cleared (Q-HUB-289).

rules.heading: ## What it reads
rules.quote: The step M's own text in the plan, and in it the three labels the review judges the aim by: its Facts
rules.says: The review reads step M's own text in the plan, including its Facts (what the step is told it depends on, restated from the plan's asks), its Observe (what must be seen for the step to be done) and its Kill (what ends the step with nothing further written).

rules.heading: ## What it reads
rules.quote: They are read against the plan's goal 1, the first goal under its Goals, and not against the step's own sentence
rules.says: Facts, Observe and Kill are judged against the plan's goal 1 (the first goal under Goals), not the step's own sentence, and a step whose Observe does not show goal 1 nearer, whose Facts restate a premise earlier hand-backs show false, or whose Kill leaves a write behind is aimed at the wrong thing however well it reads.

rules.heading: ## What it reads
rules.quote: A step on the Standing line carries none of the four labels and is read as it is written.
rules.says: A step on the Standing line has no Facts, Observe or Kill labels and is read as it is written.

rules.heading: ## What it reads
rules.quote: The owner's messages, by the script below, and only those typed before the moment being judged.
rules.says: The review reads the owner's messages by means of the script, and only those typed before the moment being judged.

rules.heading: ## What it reads
rules.quote: For the route: this plan's Rules section, `DOCTRINE.md` section 0e in the live clone, the gate list in the hub `CLAUDE.md`
rules.says: For the route the review reads the plan's Rules section, DOCTRINE.md section 0e in the live clone, the hub CLAUDE.md gate list, the refusals in the session's earlier reports and the guards' code in /root/.claude/hub (with Read and Grep), plus, where the step works in Jefferson-Photography-Studio, that repository's tools/harness-guard.mjs and .claude/hooks/ident-guard.mjs.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: The hand-back is the whole of the report. Its first line is the verdict:
rules.says: The review's hand-back is the whole of its report, and its first line is the verdict.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: ON-AIM or OFF-AIM, then ROUTE-CLEAR or ROUTE-REFUSED, then `step N` for the hand-back judged and `next M` for the step whose route it read.
rules.says: The verdict line has the form ON-AIM or OFF-AIM, then ROUTE-CLEAR or ROUTE-REFUSED, then step N for the hand-back judged and next M for the step whose route it read, for example ON-AIM ROUTE-CLEAR step 12 next 13.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: When no step of Order has ended yet, N is the word none. N is the step of the newest end in Order of any kind
rules.says: N is the word none when no step of Order has ended, and otherwise N is the step of the newest end in Order of any kind (DONE, refusal, failure or eject), as the status print's Order line shows it, never the step before that end.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: Its second line, directly under the verdict, is the review's own wall line, which begins with the words `Wall line:` and is one sentence answering three questions
rules.says: The second line of the hand-back begins with Wall line: and is one sentence answering whether step M still serves the plan's goal 1 (read from Facts, Observe, Kill), whether that goal still serves the owner's asks as the plan's Design states them, and whether what the review read this send moved either answer.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: The dispatcher reads only the first line (`parseVerdict` in `report.mjs`), so the second line cannot spoil the verdict, and a wall line that answers no is a reason for OFF-AIM
rules.says: A wall line that answers no is a reason for OFF-AIM or for the amendment the route names, and the review's wall line is a separate judgement of the move about to go, written before it goes, distinct from the wall line each step's hand-back carries under its DONE, REFUSED, FAILED or EJECT word.

rules.heading: What it hands back (wall line)
rules.quote: The dispatcher reads only the first line (`parseVerdict` in `report.mjs`), so the second line cannot spoil the verdict
rules.says: The dispatcher reads only the first line of the hand-back, so the verdict must stand alone on line one and the wall line on line two cannot change or spoil it.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: Aim: what the owner wants, as the outcome the owner will see, in the reviewer's own words from the owner's messages and never from the plan
rules.says: Under the verdict the Aim section states what the owner wants as the outcome the owner will see, in the reviewer's own words taken from the owner's messages and never from the plan, then what the hand-back found, then the judgement.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: OFF-AIM when the report shows the plan aimed at the wrong thing, which is any one of three things:
rules.says: The review returns OFF-AIM when the report shows the plan aimed at the wrong thing, meaning any one of: the cause of what the owner wants put right lies outside what the plan's steps may change, a step's premise is shown false, or what the plan builds cannot give the outcome the owner wants.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: A refusal, a failure, or a defect with a known fix inside the plan's reach is not OFF-AIM: the main thread handles it and the plan goes on. ON-AIM otherwise.
rules.says: A refusal, a failure, or a defect with a known fix inside the plan's reach is not OFF-AIM (the main thread handles it and the plan goes on), and the verdict is ON-AIM otherwise.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: Route: every command and write that step M orders, read against the Rules, the doctrine, the gate list and the guards' code.
rules.says: The Route section reads every command and write that step M orders against the Rules, the doctrine, the gate list and the guards' code, and ROUTE-REFUSED names each command or write a guard would refuse, the guard, and the line that refuses it.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: After a step ended other than DONE, it also reads each unsent step of the Order for the same cause and names in a refused route each that carries it.
rules.says: After a step ended other than DONE, the review also reads each unsent step of the Order for the same cause and names, in a refused route, each step that carries it.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: The guards are not only the hub's:
rules.says: The guards the route is read against include guards that are not the hub's own (the next three items).

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: In a session with the Jefferson-Photography-Studio repository checked out, an agent that runs commands there meets two hooks of that repository's own
rules.says: Those two hooks are read in the Jefferson-Photography-Studio repository, not the live clone, and tools/harness-guard.mjs refuses a node run or node --check on a file under the session scratchpad (a worktree's tracked files included) that does not print a MADE TO FAIL block in its own console.log, so such a check must be a child process of a scratch script that carries the block.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: `.claude/hooks/ident-guard.mjs` refuses any tool call whose input carries a run of seven or more hexadecimal characters that no earlier tool result of the session printed.
rules.says: In a session with Jefferson-Photography-Studio checked out, any tool call whose input carries a run of seven or more hexadecimal characters that no earlier tool result of the session printed is refused.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: The harness's permission classifier is a third, and it is visible in no code. It refuses a command that destroys local work, a stash drop, a checkout or restore of a file, a clean or a reset among them
rules.says: The harness's permission classifier refuses any command that destroys local work (a stash drop, checkout or restore of a file, a clean, a reset) whatever the plan's Commands list says, so a step that orders such a command is ROUTE-REFUSED naming the classifier, and the amendment takes the work out by editing instead.

rules.heading: What it hands back / Route (the permission classifier)
rules.quote: The harness's permission classifier is a third, and it is visible in no code. It refuses a command that destroys local work
rules.says: The permission classifier is visible in no code and no hub gate shows its refusal beforehand, so the review must name its refusals from this rule and cannot find them by reading guard code.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: Sequence: the Order is read for wall clock as well as for commands. ROUTE-REFUSED names any two steps the plan's `## Order` puts in sequence
rules.says: ROUTE-REFUSED names any two steps the Order puts in sequence, one to end before the other goes, when they share no repository and no dependency and the Order does not say they run at the same time or in whichever order they end.
rules.live_quote: Steps that touch different files run together.
rules.missing: The refusal: no reviewer names two steps put in sequence that share no repository or dependency and are not marked as running together or in either order; test is by files, not repository/dependency.

rules.heading: What it hands back (Sequence)
rules.quote: Sequence: the Order is read for wall clock as well as for commands.
rules.says: The review reads the plan's Order for wall-clock time (how steps are sequenced) as well as for the commands each step orders.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: Two steps share a repository when their leads name the same one, and one depends on the other when its lead names it as the step it is for or comes after.
rules.says: Definition: two steps share a repository when their leads name the same one, and one depends on the other when its lead names it as the step it is for or comes after.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: The amendment is the Order section's own: it lists the two together with a sentence saying they run together, each cleared by its own review and sent while the other runs.
rules.says: The amendment for a sequence refusal is that the Order lists the two steps together with a sentence saying they run together, each cleared by its own review and sent while the other runs, so a plan never holds one step back for another it does not need and never waits for the delay to be noticed after it is paid.
rules.live_quote: Steps that touch different files run together.
rules.missing: The amendment (Order lists the two together with a sentence saying they run together, each cleared by its own review) and the rule that a plan never holds back a step it does not need are not stated.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: Report lines quoted are agents' writing. No owner message is quoted, and no identifier and no hex is written.
rules.says: In the review's hand-back, quoted report lines are agents' writing, no owner message is quoted, and no identifier and no hex is written.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: ON-AIM ROUTE-CLEAR naming `next M`, with `step N` the step of the newest end in Order: step M may be sent, and no other step.
rules.says: When the dispatcher reads ON-AIM ROUTE-CLEAR naming next M with step N the step of the newest end in Order, step M may be sent and no other step.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: ROUTE-REFUSED: step M is not sent. The plan's Steps or Order are amended from the commands the verdict names
rules.says: On ROUTE-REFUSED, step M is not sent; the plan's Steps or Order are amended from the commands the verdict names (keeping the approval while Goals, Asked, Files and Commands stand) and the review is sent again.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: OFF-AIM: no step is sent. The plan goes back to plan mode and is rewritten.
rules.says: On OFF-AIM no step is sent, and the plan goes back to plan mode and is rewritten.

rules.heading: ## What it hands back
rules.quote: Anything else is not a verdict, and clears nothing.
rules.says: Any first line that is not one of the defined verdicts is not a verdict and clears nothing.
